steps.text: Using dial indicator, check camshaft end play. Camshaft end play must not be more than 0.012-in. (0.3 mm). If end play exceeds specification, camshaft sprocket (4), thrust plate (7), and spacer must be inspected for wear after removal.

Measure inside diameter of all camshaft bearings (2). Number one through number four camshaft bearings must be 2.167-2.170 in. (55.041-55.118 mm) and number five camshaft bearing (rear) must be 2.009-2.012-in. (51.028-51.104 mm). If any camshaft bearings (2) do not meet specifica- tions, replace all camshaft bearings (2) (para. 2-16.d.3) and hot tank clean cylinder block (1) (para. 2-16.b.1).
If all bearings (2) are to be reused, steam clean cylinder block (1) (para. 2-16.b.2).

Steam cleaning.

notes.text: Compressed air used for cleaning purposes will not exceed 30 psi (207 kPa). Use only with effective chip guarding and personal protective equipment (goggles/shield, gloves, etc.).

steps.text: Inspect all surfaces and general overall condition of the cylinder block (1).

notes.text: • For general inspection instructions, refer to para. 2-10.

steps.text: Visually check the cylinder block (1) for pitting in cylinder walls (4) and lifter bores (2). Replace engine if pitted or distorted.
Inspect the cylinder block (1) for cracks in cylinder walls (4), water jacket (5), lifter bores (2), and main bearing webs (8). Replace engine if cracked.
Inspect main bearing caps (6) for cracks, scoring, or damage. Replace engine if any are cracked, scored, or damaged.
Inspect main bearing cap bolts (7) for damage. Replace if damaged.
Inspect dowel pins (3) for damage. Replace if damaged.

Using a straightedge and feeler gauge, check flatness of cylinder head sealing surfaces on cylinder block (1). Flatness on cylinder block (1) must not vary more than 0.002 in. (0.051 mm) in a distance of 6 in. (15.2 mm) or more than 0.006 in. (0.152 mm) overall. Repair cylinder or replace engine if flatness does not meet above specifications.

Using cylinder bore gauge, measure all cylinder bores (2) for taper. Measurements must be taken at point “A” (4) at top and bottom of cylinder bore (2). If any cylinder exceeds specifications (table 2-2 or 2-3) by 0.005 in. (0.127 mm) or more, repair cylinder or replace engine.

Remove cover (1) and gasket (13). Discard gasket (13).

notes.text: If fuel is found in pump, discard fuel in an approved container.

steps.text: Remove cap (8) from guide stud (7). Using 1/4-in. hex head driver, remove guide stud (7), seal (5), and nut (6) from min-max governor (12). Discard seal (5) and cap (8).

notes.text: • Perform steps 5, 6, and 7 for 6.5L engines and 6.2L engines 1990 and above.

steps.text: Turn throttle shaft (11) to low idle and remove idle spring (16).

Turn throttle shaft (11) to wide open throttle, loosen sleeve (17) on min-max governor (12) and lift min-max governor (12) and inner governor spring (14) out of pump (9) and disengage min-max governor (12) from governor thrust spring (15).
Using 1/4-in. hex head driver, remove guide stud (7) and washer (10) from min-max governor (12). Discard washer (10).
Turn throttle shaft (11) to wide open throttle and pull min-max governor (12) out of pump (9).
Deleted.

Remove two retaining clips (15) from rocker lever pin (16). Discard clips (15).

Using Torx drive, remove screw (14) from face cam (8) and remove face cam (8) and washer (7) from throttle shaft (1).
Turn throttle shaft (1) to low idle and release the governor thrust spring (5) from housing boss (6).

notes.text: • Perform steps 15 and 16 for 6.5L engines and for 6.2L engines 1990 and above.

Remove throttle shaft (1) from housing (4), and remove two O-rings (3) and spacer (2) from throttle shaft (1). Discard O-rings (3).
Hold metering valve (19) and raise governor linkage hook (17) from valve arm pin (18).
Hold governor arm (22) forward and pull linkage hook (17) back and detach from governor arm (22).
Remove linkage hook (17), governor arm (22), and spring (21) from housing (4).
Remove spring (21) from linkage hook (17) and governor arm (22).
Remove metering valve (19) from housing (4).

Using end cap wrench, remove fuel pump end cap (9) from hydraulic head (20).

notes.text: Early production injection pumps have an inlet filter screen, retaining ring, and seal or pressure plate. Late production pumps have a different configuration screen which does not require a retaining ring and seal or pressure plate. When repairing early production pumps, replace the screen with a late production one.

steps.text: Remove retaining ring (12) and screen (11) from pressure plate (10), if applicable.

Remove inlet filter screen seal (16), end plate adjusting plug (13), spring (14), and piston (15) from regulator (17). Discard adjusting plug (13) and seal (16). Tag spring (14) and piston (15) for assembly.
Remove transfer pump liner (7), four blades (18), and two springs (6).
Remove head-locking capscrews (1) and (21) from housing (22).
Rotate housing (22) and holding fixture in vise so advance plug (28) faces upward.
Using 5/16-in. hex head driver, remove head locating screw (27) and O-ring (26). Discard O-ring (26).
Remove spring side plug assembly (24) and O-ring (25) from housing (22). Disard O-ring (25).
Remove servo advance plunger (23) from spring side plug (24).
Using 1/4-in. hex head driver, remove advance plug (28), cam advance pin (30), and O-ring (29) from housing (22). Discard O-ring (29).
Remove power side advance piston hole plug (35) and O-ring (34). Discard O-ring (34).
Remove servo advance piston assembly (33) from housing (22). Tap piston assembly (33) to remove spring (31) and valve (32). Tag spring (31) for assembly.
Rotate housing (9) and holding fixture right side up.
Remove head locking capscrew (1).
Remove hydraulic head assembly (7) from housing (9).
Remove six weights (8), washer (3), and governor thrust sleeve (2) from hydraulic head (7).
Remove liner locating ring (4) and two rotor retainers (5) from hydraulic head (7).
Remove transfer pump end cap seal (6) from hydraulic head (7). Discard seal (6).
Remove snapring (10) and weight retainer (11) from rotor (13).
Remove cam ring (12) from hydraulic head (7).

Remove leaf spring adjusting screw (7) and leaf spring (6) from rotor (4).

Install governor weight support in vise.

steps.text: Inspect housing (5) for damage. Replace injection pump if damaged.

notes.text: For general inspection instructions, refer to para. 2-10.

steps.text: Inspect pilot tube (4) in housing (5) for scoring or damage. If scored or damaged, perform steps 3 through 7, if not, go to step 8.
Remove pilot tube (4) and drive shaft bearing (3) from housing (5) using pilot tube mandrel. Discard pilot tube (4).
Inspect drive shaft bearing (3) for roughness or damage. Discard if rough or damaged.
Apply sealing compound to outside diameter of pilot tube (4).
Using pilot tube mandrel, install pilot tube (4) in housing (5) until groove (6) in pilot tube (4) aligns with vent hole (7) in housing (5).
Using drive shaft bearing installer, install drive shaft bearing (3) in housing (5). Go to step 11.
Inspect drive shaft bearing (3) for roughness or damage. If rough or damaged, perform steps 9 and 10. If not, go to step 11.
Remove drive shaft bearing (3) from housing (5) and discard bearing (3).
Using drive shaft bearing installer, install driveshaft bearing (3) in housing (5).
Inspect throttle shaft bushings (1) for damage. If damaged, perform steps 12 through 20 using throttle and shutoff shaft bushing installation kit. If not, go to step 21.
Install brace into housing (2) to prevent distortion of housing (2) during bushing (1) removal.
Install rod through bushings (1).
Install bushing guide, two washers, and nuts.
Tighten nuts until bushing (1) is removed from housing (2). Remove tools and discard bushing (1).
Install brace and rod into housing (2).
Apply sealing compound to outside diameter of bushing (1).
Install bushing (1), bushing guide, two washers, and nuts on rod.
Tighten nuts until bushing (1) is past flush with bushing boss (3) on housing (2). Remove tools from housing (2).
Repeat steps 12 through 19 for opposite bushing, if required.
Inspect idle spring (2) on min-max governor (1) for corrosion or damage. Replace if corroded or damaged.
Inspect inner governor spring (7) for corrosion or damage. Replace if corroded or damaged.

notes.text: Perform steps 22 and 23 for 6.5L engines and 6.2L engines 1990 and above.

steps.text: Inspect governor thrust spring (8) for corrosion or damage. Replace if corroded or damaged.
Inspect min-max spring (3) for corrosion or damage. If corroded or damaged, perform steps 25 through 29. If not, go to step 30.
Remove idle spring (2) from pushrod (5).
Measure distance “A” from throttle block (4) to end of pushrod (5) for assembly.
Put throttle block (4) in vise and remove pushrod (5), spring (3), and washer (6). Discard spring (3).
Install washer (6) and spring (3) on pushrod (5) and install into throttle block (4).
Tighten pushrod (5) until measurement taken in step 26 is obtained.
Inspect regulatar (10) for damage. Replace if damaged.
Inspect roll pin (9) in regulator (10) for damage. Replace if damaged.

notes.text: When removing roll pin, note which hole from where pin is removed, It is marked “C” or “CC”.

steps.text: Inspect arm spring (11) for damage. Replace if damaged.
Inspect metering valve (12) and arm (13) for damage. If damaged, perform steps 34 and 35. If not, go to step 36.

notes.text: Metering valves are available in standard and oversize. If replacing metering valve, check for number “SB-336” on top of hydraulic head. If number is present, oversize metering valve must be used or injection pump may malfunction.

steps.text: Place valve (12) in holding fixture hole and remove arm (13) from valve (12).
Install arm (13) on valve (12).

Using a micrometer, measure drive shaft (2) at point “A” to determine wear. Inspect drive shaft (2) seal area for nicks, burrs, scratches, or damage. Replace drive shaft (2) if measurement at point “A” is less than 0.305 in. (7.75 mm) or if any nicks, burrs, scratches, or damage is present.
Inspect dowel pin (1) in drive shaft (2) for damage. If damaged, replace dowel pin (1). Apply sealing compound to replacement dowel pin (1).
Inspect fittings (4) in hydraulic head (3) for damage. Replace hydraulic head (3) and rotor (13) if any fittings (4) are damaged.

notes.text: Hydraulic head and rotor are matched sets and must be replaced as an assembly or injection pump damage may result.

steps.text: Inspect hydraulic head (3) and rotor (13) for damage. Replace both if either is damaged.

notes.text: Do not handle precision ground surface of rotor to prevent contamination.

steps.text: Inspect charging ports (11) and discharge port (12) on rotor (13) for chipped edges. Replace hydraulic head (3) and rotor (13) if any chipped edges are apparent.
Inspect rotor (13) for scratches. Replace hydraulic head (3) and rotor (13) if scratches are present.

Inspect leaf spring contact area (14) and tang slot (7) on rotor (13) for excessive wear. Replace hydraulic head (3) and rotor (13) if leaf spring contact area (14) or tang slot (7) are excessively worn.

notes.text: Do not allow solvents to get on skin or clothing. Solvents can burn easily and give off harmful vapors. Keep away from open fire and use in a well-ventilated area. If solvent gets on skin or clothing, wash immediately. Failure to follow these instructions could cause injury or death.

It maybe necessary to interchange or reverse plunger position when installing plungers into rotor. 42, While holding rotor (13) under clean calibrating fluid, insert plungers (10) into bores of rotor (13). With thumb and forefinger over roller shoe (9) slots, tilt from side to side to determine freedom of movement. If the plungers (10) are sticking, but not visibly damaged, clean both plungers (10) and bore with a soft brush and lacquer thinner or acetone. Check freedom of movement again. If plungers (10) still stick, replace them with the next smaller size (“A” is the largest, “D” is the smallest). If the smallest plungers (10) stick in rotor (13), replace hydraulic head (3) and rotor (13).

steps.text: Inspect cam rollers (8) for freedom of rotation in their roller shoes (9). Inspect cam rollers (8) and roller shoes (9) for abrasive wear patterns. Replace cam rollers (8) and roller shoes (9) if cam rollers (8) do not rotate freely or if either shows signs of abrasive wear patterns.
Inspect top edge of each roller shoe (9) for chipping or excessive wear. Replace cam rollers (8) and roller shoes (9) if chipped or excessively worn.
Inspect leaf spring (6) for excessive wear. Replace leaf spring (6) if excessively worn.
Inspect leaf spring screw (5) for tightness in rotor (13). Replace leaf spring screw (5) if screw (5) does not thread tightly into rotor (13).
Inspect cam lobes (16) on cam ring (15) for spalling or flaking out. Replace cam ring (15) if cam lobes (16) are spalled or flaked.

notes.text: Machining marks between cam lobes should not be considered damage.

steps.text: Inspect all transfer pump blades (17) and transfer pump liner (18) for scoring or damage. Replace all transfer pump blades (17) and transfer pump liner (18) if any are scored or damaged.

Using a micrometer, measure transfer pump blades (17) at point “A” to determine wear. If any transfer blade (17) is smaller than 0.538 in. (13.67 mm), replace all transfer pump blades (17) and transfer pump liner (18).
Inspect governor weights (21) for excessive wear at heel (19) and toe (20) Replace governor weights (21) if excessively worn.
Inspect delivery valve reaction cuff (22) for chipping or erosion. Replace delivery valve (23) if reaction cuff (22) is chipped or eroded.
Inspect vent wire (25) in vent wire screw (24) for freedom of movement. If vent wire (25) is stuck, replace vent wire screw (24).
Inspect throttle shaft (3) for distortion or damage. Replace if distorted or damaged.
Install low idle screw (1), spring (2), max travel screw (4), and nut (5) in throttle shaft (3).

notes.text: Perform step 55 only if throttle shaft was replaced.

steps.text: Inspect rubber connectors (6) for deterioration, cracks, or damage. Replace if cracked, deteriorated, or damaged.
Inspect pump cover (7) for damage. Replace if damaged.
Inspect check valve (8) for damage. Replace if damaged.
Inspect cold start advance solenoid (10) for damage. Replace if damaged.
Inspect insulators (9) and plunger (11) for damage, Replace if damaged,
Inspect insulators (13) and electrical shutoff solenoid (12) for damage. Replace if damaged.
Refer to para. 2-10 for general inspection instructions for all other injection pump parts.

steps.text: Mount injection pump housing (20) in holding fixture and secure with vise.

notes.text: Handle all parts carefully with clean hands wet with calibrating fluid to avoid contamination.

steps.text: Lubricate seals (17), (18), and (19) with seal lubricant and install black seal (17) in groove (25), red seal (18) in groove (24) and black seal (19) in groove (23) using drive shaft seal installer.
Install thrust button spring (15) and thrust button (14) in drive shaft assembly (16).
Install drive shaft assembly (16) in housing (20).

notes.text: Note position of timing mark on end of drive shaft tang when installing drive shaft assembly. This is necessary to align rotor to drive shaft.

steps.text: Install snapring (21) in groove (22) on drive shaft assembly (16).
Mount governor weight support in vise and rinse rotor (1) in calibrating fluid and install in support.

notes.text: G Do not handle precision ground surface of rotor to avoid contamination. G Handle all parts carefully with clean hands wet with calibrating fluid to avoid contamination.

steps.text: Install delivery valve (2) in rotor (1).

notes.text: . Delivery valves are available in standard and oversize. If replacing delivery valve, check for marking “OS” on side of rotor. If “OS” marking is present, oversize delivery valve must be used. G Oversize delivery valves have a black marking at the base of delivery valve.

steps.text: Install valve spring (3) and valve stop (4) in rotor (1).
Using 5/32-in. hex head driver, install stop plug (5) in rotor (1) and tighten to 85-90 lb-in. (10 N•m).

notes.text: Excessive tightening of stop plug will cause seizure of hydraulic head and rotor.

steps.text: Install leaf spring (9) and adjusting screw (10) on rotor (1).
Remove rotor (1) from governor weight support and submerge in calibrating fluid.
Install two plungers (8) in rotor (1).

notes.text: G Plungers of any given nominal diameter are graded in four select fit sizes: A, B, C, and D. The rotor is etched with the letter indi- cating bore size. This mark is found on the base of the rotor. G If plunger replacement is required, check the size designation on the rotor and use the plunger of corresponding part number as indicated by letter designation on rotor.

steps.text: Assemble two cam roller shoes (7), and cam rollers (6), and install in rotor (1).
Install roller-to-roller setting tool in soft-jaw vise.
Install roller (1) in roller-broiler setting tool.
Apply compressed air regulated to 40-100 psi (276-689 kPa) to roller-broiler setting tool.

notes.text: Always wear eyeshields when using compressed air. Failure to wear eyeshields may result in eye injury.

steps.text: Measure roller-to-roller dimension and compare to pump specification 1.981 in. (50.31 mm).

notes.text: Increase roller-to-roller dimension 0.006 in. (0.152 mm) if using oversize cam ring.

steps.text: Turn leaf spring adjusting screw (2) clockwise to increase or counterclockwise to decrease roller- to-roller dimension.

notes.text: Roller-to-roller dimension is a completely accurate maximum fuel adjustment and should not differ from pump specification.

steps.text: Rotate rotor (1) until one cam roller (3) aligns with roller-to-roller setting tool dial indicator plunger.

Loosen indicator dial retaining screw and set preload by sliding indicator down until plunger depresses on cam roller (3) 0.015 in. (0.381 mm). Tighten screw. Rotate dial on indicator to “zero” indicator on high point of cam roller (3). 21.

Measure cam roller centrality by rotating rotor (1) in either direction until high point of other cam roller (3) depressed dial indicator plunger. Indicator reading should be 0.000 in. to 0.008 in. (0.000 to 0.203 mm).

notes.text: If cam roller centrality is greater than 0.008 in. (0.203 mm), cam shoes can be interchanged or replaced to achieve tolerance. Centrality must be rechecked after each time components are changed.

steps.text: Rinse hydraulic head (4) with calibrating fluid.
Remove rotor (1) from roller-to-roller setting tool and rinse with calibrating fluid.
Install rotor (1) in hydraulic head (4).
Install head seal (5) on rotor (4).
Install cam ring (8) on hydraulic head (4) with directional arrow on ring showing counterclockwise rotation of pump rotor (1).
Install weight retainer (7) on rotor (1), align with check ball, and secure with snapring (6).
Install transfer pump end cap seal (2) in hydraulic head (1).
Install two rotor retainers (3) with cut out portions meeting over roll pin hole in hydraulic head (1).

notes.text: Use care when handling rotor weight retainer and hydraulic head before retainers are installed. Rotor can fall out and cause damage to components.

steps.text: Install liner locating ring (4) on hydraulic head (1) with split 90° from roll pin hole.
Install transfer pump liner (5) so slot aligns with roll pin hole in hydraulic head (1).
Install two springs (6) in four transfer pump blades (7) and install transfer pump blades (7) in rotor (8).

notes.text: Blades must not be cocked during installation. Sharp edge of liner can score blade ends.

G Transfer pump blades are available in standard and oversize. Oversize blades are marked in black and must be used whenever possible. G Oversize and standard transfer pump blades do not have to be used as matched sets.

steps.text: Install piston (10), spring (13), and adjusting plug (11) in regulator (9). Tighten adjusting plug (11) until flush with end of regulator (9).

notes.text: Adjusting plug must not be installed past flush with end of regulator or pump damage will result.

notes.text: Early production injection pumps have an inlet filter screen, retaining ring, and seal or pressure plate. Late production pumps have a different configuration screen which does not require a retaining ring and seal or pressure plate. When repairing early production pumps, replace the screen with a late production one.

steps.text: Install filter screen (12) on regulator (9).
Lightly coat filter screen assembly (14) and threads of transfer end cap (16) with seal lubricant.
Install filter screen assembly (14) and end cap (16) on hydraulic head (1). Apply slight pressure on top of end cap (16) and rotate counterclockwise until a slight click is heard.
Turn end cap (16) clockwise until snug.
Install inlet tube assembly (15) on end cap (16).
Install six governor weights (3) in weight retainer (4).
Install thrust washer (2) and thrust sleeve (1) into lower slots of governor weights (3).

notes.text: Governor weights must work freely after installation.

steps.text: Align timing mark (11) on drive shaft (5) and timing mark (6) on rotor (7).
Apply light coat of seal lubricant to inside edge of housing (12).
Rotate cam ring (9) so index mark (11) is aligned with timing cover access hole (13).
Install hydraulic head (10) in housing (12) with slight rotary motion.

notes.text: Hydraulic head must only be installed far enough to install head locking screws, or leakage and damage to hydraulic head O-ring seal will result.

steps.text: Rotate head (10) and align head locking capscrew holes with holes in housing (12).
Install two head locking capscrews (8) finger tight.
Install O-ring (6) on head locating screw (7).
Lightly coat head locating screw (7) with seal lubricant and install in housing (11). Tighten screw (7) to 180-220 lb-in. (20-25 N•m) using 5/16-in. hex head driver.
Install cam advance pin (10).

notes.text: Rotate cam ring to align hole for cam advance pin in housing.

steps.text: Install O-ring (9) and advance plug (8) in housing (11). Tighten advance plug (8) with 1/4-in. hex head driver to 75-100 lb-in. (9-11 N•m).
Install servo advance valve (5) on spring (4) and install servo advance valve (5) in servo advance piston (14).
Install servo advance plunger (1) and O-ring (3) on spring side plug (2).
Install spring side plug assembly (2) in housing (11) so servo advance plunger (1) fits in spring (4). Tighten sprinig side plug assembly (2) to 215-265 lb-in. (24-30 N•m).
Rotate housing (11) and holding fixture 180°
Install vent wire screw (18). Tighten to 25-30 lb-in. (3 N•m) with 1/8-in. hex head driver.

notes.text: The vent wire screw is available in different sizes (identification numbers are etched on each) to adjust return oil flow. If original screw is to be replaced, use the same size. The final determination will be made during calibration.

steps.text: Install metering valve assembly (17) in housing (11).
Connect linkage hook (15) to governor arm (20).
Install spring (19) on governor arm (20) and linkage hook (15).
Install governor arm (20) in housing (11) so that feet on governor arm (20) fit in slots in thrust sleeve (21).

notes.text: Governor arm must be installed correctly or injection pump will malfunction.

steps.text: Install linkage hook (15) on valve arm pin (16).
Install spacer (2) and two O-rings (3) on throttle shaft (1) and install throttle shaft (1) in housing (4).

notes.text: • Perform step 66 for pre-1990 engines.

Install mylar washer (6) and face cam (7) on throttle shaft (1) with screw (13). Finger tighten screw (13).
Install rocker lever (12) on housing (4) with rocker lever pin (15) and two retaining clips (14).
Put 0.005-in. (0.127 mm) feeler gauge between throttle shaft mylar washer (6) and housing boss (16).

Put throttle shaft (1) in idle position. Squeeze throttle shaft (1) and face cam (7) tightly toward each other and rotate face cam (7) so lower roller rests approximately in middle of low idle step. Tighten screw (13) to 30 lb-in. (3 N•m) with Torx drive and remove feeler gauge.
Align holes in kickdown cam (10) and throttle shaft (1).
Install kickdown cam (10) on throttle shaft (1) with retaining pin (9).
Deleted.
Install idle spring (1) on pushrod (2).

notes.text: Tightly wound coils on idle spring must be installed facing throttle block, or injection pump may malfunction.

steps.text: With throttle shaft (8) in wide open position, install min-max governor (4) on notch of throttle shaft (8). Rotate throttle shaft (8) to low idle position and lower min-max governor (4) into housing (5).

Hook tang (10) of thrust spring (11) in groove (13) of housing (5).

notes.text: Guide stud must be installed between metering valve arm and spring. Incorrect installation may cause injection pump to malfunction.

Install O-ring (15) and check valve (1) in cover (2).
Install plunger (10) in cold start advance solenoid (9) and stud (11) in hole in rear of cover (2).
Install cold start advance solenoid (9) in cover (2) so small tip of plunger (10) fits in port of check valve (1) and stud (8) fits through hole inside of cover (2).

Install fiber washer (3), washer (4), lockwasher (5), and nut (6) on stud (11).
Install shell (12), washer (13), and terminal (14) on stud (11).
Install electrical shutoff solenoid (9) in cover (11).
Install fiber washer (7), washer (6), lockwasher (5), nut (4), lockwasher (12), ground strap (13) and locknut (14) on stud (10).
Install fiber washer (7), washer (6), lockwasher (5), and nut (4) on stud (8).
Install shell (3), washer (2), and terminal (1) on stud (8).
Install washer (15) between ground strap (16) and cover (11).
Install gasket (31) and cover (11) on housing (30) and secure with three screws (17), lock- washers (18), and washers (19). Tighten screws (17) to 35-45 lb-in. (4-5 N•m).

notes.text: When installing cover on housing, cover must be positioned on housing ahead of threaded holes and slid rearward to align holes in cover with threaded holes in housing. Incorrect installation of cover may cause pump to malfunction.

steps.text: Install timing cover (28) and gasket (27) on housing (30) and secure with two screws (29).
Using end cap wrench, tighten end cap (26) to 30-37 lb-ft (41-50 N•m).

Install transfer pump end cap locking screw (25), plate (24), flat washer (23), and rubber washer (22) in hydraulic head (21). Tighten screw (25) to 70-80 lb-in. (8-9 N•m) using 5/32-in. hex head driver.
Tighten two head locking capscrews (20) to 180-220 lb-in. (20-25 N•m).
Remove pump (30) from holding fixture and vise.

procedures.title: (6.2L or 6.5L) fuel injection pumps (DB2829-4523, DB2829-4879, or DB2831-5149) calibration using fuel injection pump test stand (FTIS) model A8022

steps.text: Insert alignment gauge into test stand drive coupling.
Install fuel injection pump (1) on adapter plate (6) and secure with three 5/16-in. washers (3) and 5/16-18x1 hex-head capscrews (2).
Position fuel injection pump (1), with flange mounting bracket (5) installed, to test stand drive coupling.
Using barring tool, rotate driveshaft (12) until tapped holes on pump-mounted drive hub (7) are aligned with slots in test stand drive coupling.

Install three 3/8-in. washers (8), 3/8-in. lockwashers (9), and 3/8-16x1 hex-head capscrews (10) in slots and mounting holes on test stand drive coupling and pump-mounted drive hub (7). Remove barring tool.
Tighten two 3/8-16x1 hex-head capscrews (4) that secure flange mounting bracket (5) to bedplate (11). Remove alignment gauge.
Install test adapter and connector on fuel inlet port (2) of fuel injection pump (1).
Connect one end of hose assembly to connector and insert other hose end into calibration fluid supply quick-connect on front panel of test stand (3).
Remove screw (8), tab (7), washer (6), and O-ring (5) from fuel injection pump transfer port (4).
Position test adapter on fuel injection pump transfer test port (4) and secure into position with existing O-ring (5), tab (7), and washer (6) removed in step 9.
Install quick-connect plug into test adapter.
Connect one end of rubber hose assembly (9) to quick-connect plug and other hose assembly end to auxiliary pressure quick-connect on front panel of test stand (3).
Install male pipe fitting on fuel injection pump (1).

Connect one end of tubing to male pipe fitting on fuel injection pump (1) and other end to calibration fluid push-on connector on front panel of test stand (3). C A U T I O N When installing high-pressure delivery lines on fuel injection pump, use two wrenches to prevent damage to discharge fittings.
Install eight high-pressure delivery lines on discharge fittings (10) of fuel injection pump (1).

Position throttle arm positioner assembly (3) on bedplate (7) and throttle lever (1). NOT E When installing advance indicator, ensure the flat on pointer end engages into the cam ring slot on fuel injection pump.
Remove two screws (6), timing cover (5), and gasket (4) from fuel injection pump (2) and install advance indicator with two screws (6).
Remove screw plug from advance indicator block and install quick-connect on advance indicator block (8).
Attach one end of rubber hose assembly to quick-connect and the other hose assembly end to auxiliary pressure quick-connect plug on front panel of test stand.

Connect positive red test lead to DC power supply socket marked (+) on test stand, and attach the alligator clip end of red test lead to the electric shutoff solenoid terminal (9) on fuel injection pump (2).
Connect black lead to DC black socket marked “P” on test stand and connect alligator clip end of black lead to ground terminal (10) on fuel injection pump (2).

After installation and hookup of the fuel injection pump has been completed, inspect pump, all hoses, and related hardware connections before beginning pump calibration. Review operation test procedures for the FTIS prior to calibrating the fuel injection pump.
Stroke
Pump Rotation Selector
Set test stand in accordance with the following checklist and instructions in steps 2 through 25.
Set fuel injection pump per calibration chart specifications and settings in para. 2-33, 2-34, or 2-35.
Secure throttle positioner arm in Wide Open Throttle (WOT) position.
Turn calibration fluid pressure regulator fully counterclockwise.
Press calibration fluid system on pushbutton.

Adjust calibration fluid pressure regulator knob clockwise until 4.5-5.5 psi (31-38 kPa) is indicated on the Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) monitor. Apply 17.6 volts by adjusting the variable DC voltage supply knob to energize the electric shutoff solenoid.

Turn on main drive system by pressing main drive on pushbutton and holding button depressed for a minimum of three seconds. Increase pump speed to approximately 150 rpm to prime transfer pump and bleed air from the high-pressure fuel line nuts at each test nozzle.

notes.text: Be aware that under no circumstances should the transfer pump pressure exceed 130 psi (896 kPa). Excess pressure will damage pump.

steps.text: Increase pump speed to 1000 rpm. Ensure throttle lever is secured in WOT position. Run pump approximately 10 minutes to warm the calibration fluid to 110°-115°F (43.3°-46.1°C) and bleed all air from test stand and fuel pump. Observe transfer pump pressure reading on CRT monitor. It should be 70-76 psi (483-524 kPa).
If transfer pump pressure does not read 70-76 psi (483-524 kPa), decrease pump speed to 0 rpm and turn off main drive and calibration fluid systems. Disconnect hose at hydraulic head fuel inlet port.

Adjust transfer pump pressure with 74-1137 5/32-in. Allen screw-driver (74-8032 adapter kit, slot 3, or equivalent) and reconnect hose. This pressure setting is critical. Repeat test and adjust until transfer pump pressure is within limits.
Check pump return flow. With pump speed at 1000 rpm WOT, pump return flow meter should read 225-375 cc/minute. Perform adjustment if necessary.

Reduce pump speed to 325 rpm. Move throttle lever to LOW IDLE position and secure. The average flow reading on CRT monitor should be 10-18 mm 3/stroke. If flow is not correct, adjust low-idle screw or MIN-MAX governor setting to obtain proper flow.

With pump speed still at 325 rpm, and throttle lever secured in low-idle position, check/adjust variable DC voltage to 17.6 volts as follows: (a) Connect positive red test lead to cold-advance solenoid terminal. Housing pressure reading on CRT monitor should be 0-1 psi (0-7 kPa). (b) Disconnect positive red test lead from cold-advance solenoid terminal. Reduce variable DC voltage to 0 volts. Reconnect red test lead to shutoff solenoid terminal. Reduce pump speed to 200 rpm. (c) Slowly increase variable DC voltage and note voltage at which time the solenoid pulls in by listening for a clicking sound from the shutoff solenoid. (That indicates proper operation.) The shutoff solenoid should pull in with a maximum of 17.6 volts applied.
Reduce pump speed to 75 rpm. Move throttle lever to WOT position and secure. Average flow reading on CRT monitor must be a minimum of 28 mm 3/stroke.

Increase pump speed to 200 rpm with throttle lever secured in WOT position. Average flow reading on CRT monitor must be a minimum of 47 mm 3/stroke. Disconnect positive red test lead from solenoid shutoff terminal. The average flow reading on CRT monitor must be 4 mm 3/stroke maximum. Reconnect positive red test lead to shutoff solenoid terminal.

Increase pump speed to 325 rpm. Move throttle lever to LOW IDLE position and secure. Average flow reading on CRT monitor should be 10-18 mm 3/stroke with a minimum of 1.5 degree cam movement on advance indicator. Connect positive red test lead to cold-advance solenoid terminal. Housing pressure reading on CRT monitor should be 0-1 psi (0-7 kPa) with a minimum of 2.75 degree cam movement on advance indicator. Reconnect positive red test lead to shutoff solenoid terminal.

Increase pump speed to 750 rpm. Adjust throttle lever to obtain average flow reading on CRT monitor of 21.5-23.5 mm 3/stroke and secure throttle lever. Advance indicator should have 2.25- 4.75 degree cam movement.

Increase pump speed to 1000 rpm. Move and secure throttle lever in WOT position. Average flow reading on CRT monitor should be 51.0-55.0 mm 3/stroke with 0.5-2.5 degree cam movement on advance indicator.

Increase pump speed to 1600 rpm and ensure throttle lever is secured in WOT position. There should be 4.25-7.25 degree cam movement on advance indicator. Move throttle lever to LOW IDLE position. There must be a maximum of 10.0 degree cam movement on advance indicator. Move and secure throttle lever in WOT position.
Increase pump speed to 1800 rpm and ensure throttle lever is secured in WOT position. Average flow reading on CRT monitor must be a minimum of 44.5 mm 3/stroke.
Increase pump speed to 1950 rpm and ensure throttle lever is secured in WOT position. Average flow reading on CRT monitor must be a minimum of 42.5 mm 3/stroke.

Increase pump speed to 2100 rpm and ensure throttle lever is secured in WOT position. Average flow reading on CRT monitor must be a maximum of 8 mm 3/stroke. Transfer pump pressure reading on CRT monitor must be a maximum of 135 psi (931 kPa).

Reduce pump speed to 0 rpm and secure test stand. If pump met specifications, remove from test stand and mount in holding fixture. If pump did not meet specifications, repair as necessary and proceed to calibration instructions.
Using air timing gauge, check pump timing. Set timing to -0.75 to +1.25 degree.
Shut down test stand as follows: (a) Main drive pushbutton OFF. (b) Lube pushbutton OFF. (c) Calibration fluid pushbutton OFF. (d) DC selector OFF. (e) Master power switch OFF.

steps.text: Preparation. (a) Connect fuel injection nozzle (2) to tester. (b) Connect lines to return line nipples (1).

Obtaining pressure check. (a) Open shutoff valve to pressure gauge 1/4 turn. (b) Depress lever on tester slowly. Note at what pressure the needle on pressure gauge stops. Opening pressure must be between 1,500 psi (10,343 kPa) and 1,960 psi (13,514 kPa). Replace nozzle (2) if opening pressure does not meet specifications.
Leakage test. (a) Open shutoff valve to pressure gauge one additional turn.
Chatter test. (a) Close shutoff valve to pressure gauge. (b) Depress lever on tester slowly, noting whether a chattering noise can be heard.

notes.text: Compressed air used for cleaning purposes will not exceed 30 psi (207 kPa). Use only with effective chip guarding and personal protective equipment (goggles/shield, gloves, etc.). (b) Blow-dry end of nozzle (2).

A pressure of 1,400 psi (9,653 kPa) must be maintained for 10 seconds while checking for nozzle leakage. (c) Depress lever on tester until pressure gauge reads 1,400 psi (9,653 kPa) and observe tip of nozzle (2). If a droplet forms and drops off the nozzle (2) in 10 seconds or less, replace nozzle (2).

Install bypass hose (4) on bypass hose adapter (5) and secure with hose clamp (3).
Apply sealing compound to water pump rivet (7) and install in water pump (6).

notes.text: Perform step 4 if water pump was replaced.

steps.text: Clean shaft assembly (7) and housing (2) with compressed air and wipe with clean cloth.

notes.text: G Compressed air used for cleaning purposes will not exceed 30 psi (207 kPa). Use only with effective chip guarding and personal protective equipment (goggles/shield, gloves, etc.). G Do not use compressed air to spin bearings. Spinning a dry bearing with compressed air may cause injury to personnel or damage to equipment.

steps.text: Clean all other parts in accordance with para. 2-9.

notes.text: For general inspection instructions, refer to para. 2-10.

steps.text: Inspect dust seal (10) for cracks in the seal or pieces missing from it. Replace dust seal (10) if cracked or pieces missing from it. Ensure lip of seal is facing out.
Inspect roller bearings (3) and (4) in housing assembly (2) for damage. Replace fan drive assembly if damaged.
Inspect lip seal (5) in housing assembly (2) for damage. Replace fan drive assembly if damaged.
Inspect studs (1) on housing assembly (2) for stripped threads. Replace if damaged.
Inspect seal surface (6) on shaft assembly (7) for damage. Replace fan drive assembly if damaged.
Inspect bearing (8) on shaft assembly (7) for damage. Replace fan drive assembly if damaged.

steps.text: Remove all capscrews (1) and (2) and bearing caps (3) and install upper halves of main bearings (7) in cylinder block (6).

notes.text: G Measure outside diameter of crankshaft main bearing journals to determine what thickness main bearings to install. G Main bearings are of the precision insert type and do not utilize shims for adjustment. If clearances are found to be excessive, a new bearing, both upper and lower halves, will be required. Service bearings are available in standard size and undersize. G Selective fitting of both rod and main bearing inserts is necessary in production in order to obtain close tolerances. For this reason you may find one-half of a standard insert with one half of a 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) undersize insert, which will decrease the clearance 0.0005 in. (0.013 mm) from using a full standard bearing.

steps.text: Install lower halves of main bearings (4) in bearing caps (3).
Install crankshaft (8) in cylinder block (6).
Position gauging plastic on bearing journal (5) the full width of the bearing (4) and parallel to the center line of the crankshaft (8).

notes.text: The gaging plastic shall be positioned the full width of the bearing and centered on the bearing journal when the bearing cap is installed.

steps.text: Install bearing cap (3) on cylinder block (6) with two long capscrews (1) and short capscrews (2). Tighten capscrews (1) and (2) finger tight.

notes.text: Bearing caps are numbered 1 through 5 and must be installed in correct order, starting with number 1 at front of cylinder block. Arrow on bearing cap must point forward or engine damage will result.

steps.text: Tighten all long capscrews (1) to 110 lb-ft (149 N•m). Tighten all short capscrews (2) to 100 lb-ft (136 N•m).
Remove two long capscrews (1), short capscrews (2), and bearing cap (3) from cylinder block (6).
On edge of envelope (9) there is a scale which is graduated in thousandths of an inch. Without removing gauging plastic, measure its thickness at the widest point with scale on envelope (9).

If gauging plastic tapers toward the middle or ends, there is a difference in clearance indicating taper, low spot, or irregularity of bearing or crankshaft journal. If gauging plastic indicates more than 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) taper, measure crankshaft journal with micrometer (para. 2-17). NOT E If unable to obtain the proper crankshaft journal clearance, it is acceptable to use a standard bearing with a 0.0005 in. (0.013 mm) or 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) undersize bearing to produce clearance. If unable to produce proper clearance, replace crankshaft.

If the measurement is within the specifications of 0.002-0.004 in. (0.051-0.102 mm), go to step 11. If measurement is not within specifications, a 0.0005 in. (0.013 mm) or 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) under- size bearing may produce proper bearing clearance. Replace bearings and repeat steps 4 through 10.
Repeat steps 4 through 10 for remaining main bearings.

After all main bearing clearances have been set, remove crankshaft (7) and gauging plastic and apply OE/HDO to all main bearings. Install crankshaft (7), all bearing caps (1), (2), and (3), long cap- screws (4) and short capscrews (5). Tighten long capscrews (4) and short capscrews (5) to 12 lb-ft (16 N•m).

notes.text: Crankshaft must be supported during removal and installation. Failure to support crankshaft may cause injury to personnel or damage to equipment.

Bearing caps are numbered one through five and must be installed in correct order, starting with number one at front of cylinder block. Arrow on bearing cap must point forward or engine damage will result.

steps.text: Tap crankshaft (7) rearward, then frontward; this will align main bearing thrust surfaces (6). Tighten long capscrews (4) and short capscrews (5) to 40 lb-ft (54 N•m).
Tighten all long capscrews (4) to 110 lb-ft (149 N•m). Tighten all short capscrews (5) to 100 lb-ft (136 N•m).
Rotate crankshaft (7) to ensure crankshaft (7) rotates freely.

Force the crankshaft (7) to the extreme front position and hold in place. Measure end play at the front end of the number three bearing with a feeler gauge. End play should be 0.004-0.010 in. (0.101-0.250 mm).
Remove long capscrews (4), short capscrews (5), bearing caps (1), (2), and (3), and crankshaft (7) from cylinder block (8).

notes.text: • Perform steps 17 through 24 for 6.2L engines ONLY when using a 2-piece nylon rope type rear main seal.

steps.text: Apply adhesive to seal groove in rear main bearing cap (1) and cylinder block (8).
Install rear main oil seal (9) into cylinder block (8) and rear main bearing cap (1) using seal installer.
Cut excess oil seal (9) off flush with bearing cap (1) and cylinder block (8) mounting surface.
Repeat steps 4 through 10 to ensure rear oil seal (9) did not affect rear main bearing clearance. If bearing clearance changed, remove bearing cap (1) and inspect rear oil seal (9).
Remove gauging plastic.
Install number three bearing cap (3), two long capscrews (4), and short capscrews (5). Tighten capscrews (4) and (5) to 12 lb-ft (16 N•m).
Tap crankshaft (7) rearward, then frontward; this will align main bearing thrust surfaces (6). Tighten capscrews (4) and (5) on number three bearing cap (3) to 40 lb-ft (54 N•m).
Apply thin film of sealer to rear main bearing cap (1) mating surface. Keep sealer off bearing and oil seal (9) (installed on 6.2L engines).

notes.text: Immediately install rear main bearing cap after application of sealant.

steps.text: Install rear main bearing cap (1) on cylinder block (8) with long capscrews (4), and short cap- screws (5). Tighten capscrews (4) and (5) to 40 lb-ft (54 N•m).
Install remaining bearing caps (2) on cylinder block (8) with long capscrews (4) and short capscrews (5). Tighten capscrews (4) and (5) to 40 lb-ft (54 N•m).
Evenly tighten all long capscrews (4) to 110 lb-ft (149 N•m).
Evenly tighten all short capscrews (5) to 100 lb-ft (136 N•m).
Coat rear crankshaft (7) surface with engine oil, and lightly coat lip of rear main oil seal (9) with engine oil.

notes.text: Perform steps 30 through 32 for 6.5L engines.

steps.text: Insttall rear main oil seal (9), with spring Cavity towards cylinder block (8), on crankshaft (7).
Using seal installer, drive rear main oil seal (9) in until tool bottoms against cylinder block (8) and

steps.text: Install flywheel (3) on crankshaft (4) so that converter mounting surface (2) faces outward.
Secure flywheel (3) to crankshaft (4) with six capscrews (1). Tighten capscrews (1) to 65 lb-ft (88 N•m).

steps.text: Rotate cylinder block (6) approximately 90°.
Check identification number on side of connecting rod (9) and install upper rod bearing half (7) in connecting rod (9) and lower rod bearing half (12) in corresponding rod cap (5).

notes.text: Measure outside diameter of crankshaft rod bearing journals to determine what thickness connecting rod bearings to install.

steps.text: Rotate crankshaft (4) so rod journal (13) faces outward.
Cover connecting rod bolts (8) with 3/8-in. inside diameter rubber hose.
Apply OE/HDO to piston rings (11) and piston (10).
Compress piston rings (11) with ring compressor.

notes.text: Make sure all ring gaps are staggered so they are not in line with each other or piston pin.

steps.text: Check identification number on side of connecting rod (9) and install piston (10) and connecting rod (9) into corresponding cylinder.

notes.text: G Depression on top of piston must be assembled toward outside of engine. G Starting from front of cylinder block, cylinders 1, 3, 5, and 7 are on left side and cylinders 2, 4, 6, and 8 are on right side. G For remaining pistons, rotate crankshaft so rod journal faces outward.

steps.text: Tap piston (10) into cylinder until connecting rod (9) seats on crankshaft (4) and remove rubber hoses.
Position gauging plastic on bearing journal (3) the fill width of the bearing (4) and parallel to the center line of the crankshaft.

notes.text: The gauging plastic shall be positioned the full width of the bear- ing and centered on the bearing journal when the bearing cap is installed.

steps.text: Check identification number on side of connecting rod (6) and install corresponding rod cap (2).

notes.text: Identification numbers on connecting rods and rod caps must be installed on the same side.

steps.text: Secure rod cap (2) to connecting rod (6) with two nuts (1) and tighten to 44-52 lb-ft (60-71 N•m).
Remove two nuts (1) and rod cap (2) from connecting rod (6).
Measure gauging plastic at its widest point.

If the gauging plastic tapers toward the middle or ends, there is a difference in clearance indicating taper, low spot, or irregularity of bearing or crankshaft journal. If gauging plastic indicates more than 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) taper, measure crankshaft journal with micrometer (para. 2-17).

If the measurement is within specification, 0.002-0.004 in. (0.051-0.102 mm) bearing is satisfactory. If measurement is not within specifications, a 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) undersize bearing may produce proper bearing clearance. Replace bearings and repeat steps 9 through 15.

notes.text: It is acceptable to use a standard bearing with a 0.001 in. (0.025 mm) undersize bearing to obtain the proper rod bearing clearance. If unable to produce proper clearance, replace crankshaft.

steps.text: Remove gauging plastic.
Apply OE/HDO to rod bearings. Check identification number on side of connecting rod (6) and install corresponding rod cap (2).
Secure rod cap (2) to connecting rod (6) with two nuts (1) and tighten to 44-52 lb-ft (60-71 N•m).
Rotate crankshaft (5) to ensure crankshaft (5) rotates.
Repeat steps 2 through 19 for remaining pistons and connecting rods.

steps.text: Rotate cylinder block (7) so crankshaft faces upward.
Install oil pump (8) on rear main bearing cap (6).
Install stud (1) and oil pump (8) on rear main bearing cap (6) and tighten stud (1) to 59-74 lb-ft (80-100 N•m).
Install pickup tube bracket (4) on stud (1) with nut (2). Tighten nut (2) to 35 lb-ft (48 N•m).
Tighten capscrew (5) securing pickup tube bracket (4) to pickup tube (3) to 12 lb-ft (16 N•m).

diagrams.alt: Exploded view of the oil pump, stud, pickup tube and bracket above the rear main bearing cap on the cylinder block.
diagrams.credit: US Army technical manual TM 9-2815-237-34, page 2-162

steps.text: Rotate cylinder block (7) 180°.
Apply OE/HDO to all bearing journals (12) and cam lobes (11) on camshaft (13).
Install camshaft (13) into cylinder block (7).

notes.text: Support camshaft during installation to prevent damage to camshaft bearings.

steps.text: Install spacer (10) and camshaft thrust plate (9) with two capscrews (14). Tighten capscrews (14) to 18 lb-ft (24 N•m).

notes.text: Beveled edge of spacer must seat against front bearing journal on camshaft.

steps.text: Install crankshaft sprocket (10) and camshaft sprocket (4) in timing chain (5) and align timing marks (11).
Install crankshaft sprocket (10), camshaft sprocket (4), and timing chain (5) as an assembly onto camshaft (6) and crankshaft (9).

notes.text: Timing marks on crankshaft sprocket and camshaft sprocket must remain aligned after installation or engine damage may result.

steps.text: Install pump drive gear (3) on camshaft (6) with washer (2) and capscrew (1). Tighten capscrew (1) to 55-66 lb-ft (75-90 N•m).
Apply OE/HDO to timing chain (5).

Check timing chain deflection midway between camshaft sprocket (4) and crankshaft sprocket (10). Total deflection must not exceed 0.5 in. (12.7 mm). If deflection exceeds specification, inspect cam- shaft sprocket (4) and crankshaft sprocket (10) for damage. Replace either if damaged and recheck deflection.

notes.text: Perform step 7 only if timing chain was replaced.

steps.text: Install front cover seal (19) in timing gear cover (15), ensuring lip of seal (19) faces inward.
Apply a 3/32 in. (2 mm) bead of sealer to sealing surface on timing gear cover (15), following diagram shown.
Install timing gear cover (15) on cylinder block (16) with four washers (17), capscrews (18), and short capscrews (20). Tighten four capscrews (18) and short capscrews (20) to 33 lb-ft (45 N•m).
Install baffle plate (14) in timing gear cover (15) with two capscrews (12) and nut (13). Tighten capscrews (12) and nut (13) to 33 lb-ft (45 N•m).

notes.text: Maintain 0.040 in. (1.02 mm) minimum clearance between baffle plate and pump drive gear to avoid noise.

steps.text: Install rpm sensor (22) in timing gear cover (15) with capscrew (21).

notes.text: Perform step 5 for 6.5L engines.

diagrams.alt: Exploded view of the timing gear cover, baffle plate, seal and capscrews at the front of the cylinder block, with a sealer diagram and a 6.5L rpm sensor inset.
diagrams.credit: US Army technical manual TM 9-2815-237-34, page 2-165

steps.text: Rotate cylinder block (9) 180°.
Install oil pan rear seal (7) in rear main cap (8) and apply a drop of silicone sealant at each end of seal (7).
Install engine oil pan gasket (11) on oil pan sealing surface (12) and align with capscrew holes.

notes.text: G Install oil pan immediately after application of sealant. G If applying silicone sealant, perform step 4. G If installing new engine oil pan gasket, perform step 3. G Silicone sealant can be applied with the gasket, but is not required.

steps.text: Apply a 3/16 in. (5 mm) bead of silicone sealant around two large holes (10) on cylinder block (9). Apply a 3/16 in. (5 mm) bead of silicone sealant around oil pan sealing surface (12), following diagram shown.

Install oil pan (5) on cylinder block (9) with twenty capscrews (1), two studs (4), and two large capscrews (6). Tighten studs (4) and capscrews (1) to 48-120 lb-in. (5-14 N•m) and capscrews (6) to 156-240 lb-in. (18-27 N•m).
Install drainplug (2) and washer (3) in oil pan (5). Tighten drainplug (2) to 20 lb-ft (27 N•m).

diagrams.credit: US Army technical manual TM 9-2815-237-34, page 2-166

steps.text: Install two O-rings (15) on adapter bolt (13).
Install O-ring (18) on adapter (16).
Install adapter (16) on cylinder block (9) with adapter bolt (13) and gasket (14). Tighten adapter bolt (13) to 40 lb-ft (54 N•m).
Install oil filter (17) on adapter (16). Tighten oil filter (17) until gasket contacts adapter (16) and tighten an additional 1/2 to 3/4 turn.
Coat threads on fitting (22) with pipe sealing compound and install in cylinder block (9).
Coat threads on oil pressure sending unit (21) with pipe sealing compound and install in fitting (22).
Coat threads on cooler line adapters (19) and (20) with pipe sealing compound ad insall in cylinder. block (9).

steps.text: Apply OE/HDO to pushrod (8) and install into cylinder block (1).
Install gasket (2) and adapter plate (3) on cylinder block (1) with two capscrews (4). Tighten capscrews (4) to 48-84 lb-in. (5-10 N•m).
Install gasket (5) and fuel pump (6) on adapter plate (3) with two capscrews (7). Tighten capscrews (7) to 20-30 lb-ft (27-41 N•m).

diagrams.alt: Exploded view of the fuel pump, gaskets, adapter plate, capscrews and pushrod at the side of the cylinder block.
diagrams.credit: US Army technical manual TM 9-2815-237-34, page 2-168

steps.text: Rotate cylinder block (1) 180 degrees.
Install gasket (11) and oil pump drive (10) into cylinder block (1).
Secure oil pump drive (10) with clamp (12) and capscrew (9). Tighten capscrew (9) to 25-37 lb-ft (34-50 N•m).
Install gasket (5) and injection pump (6) on timing gear cover (3).
Install accelerator cable bracket (12) on fuel injection pump (6) with two capscrews (11). Tighten capscrews (11) to 13 lb-ft (18 N•m).
Install idle return spring (8) on throttle lever (7) and accelerator cable bracket (12).
Align timing marks (4) on injection pump (6) and timing gear cover (3).
Install injection pump (6) to timing gear cover (3) with three washers (10) and nuts (9).
Rotate crankshaft until timing mark (14) on pump drive gear (13) is straight up.
Align timing marks (14) on pump drive gear (13) and pump driven gear (2) and install driven gear (2) into timing gear cover (3).
Install three capscrews (1) on driven gear (2) and tighten capscrews (1) to 13-20 lb-ft (18-27 N•m).

procedures.title: Engine assembly from subassemblies
procedures.section: m. Water Pump and Adapter Plate

steps.text: Install gasket (16) and water pump (15) on adapter plate (17) with seven capscrews (18). Tighten capscrews (18) to 13-20 lb-ft (18-27 N•m).

notes.text: Ensure water pump P/N 23500085 is used on 6.5 L engines or damage to equipment will result.

steps.text: Apply sealer to sealing surfaces on adapter plate (17), following diagram shown.
Apply pipe sealing compound to capscrews (24) and (23).
Install adapter plate (17) and water pump (15) on timing gear cover (3) with two long studs (25), short stud with thick hex (21), stud (22), and capscrew (24).

Install two long capscrews (23), studs (19), four washers (20), and capscrews (26). Tighten studs (19) and capscrews (26) and (23) to 13-20 lb-ft (18-27 N•m). Tighten studs (21), (22), and (25), and capscrew (24) to 24-37 lb-ft (34-50 N•m).
Install oil fill tube (29) on adapter plate (17) with two washers (28) and nuts (27). Tighten nuts (27) to 13-20 lb-ft (18-27 N•m). SEALER DIAGRAM

steps.text: Submerge eight lifters (3) in clean diesel fuel or kerosene and work plunger (2) up and down with pushrod (1) to prime lifters (3).

notes.text: Diesel fuel is highly flammable. Do not perform this procedure near fire, flame, or sparks. Severe injury or death may result.

steps.text: Apply OE/HDO to lifters (3).
Install lifters (3) into cylinder block (7).
Install four guide plates (6) on lifters (3).
Install two guide plate clamps (4) with two capscrews (5). Tighten capscrews (5) to 15-20 lb-ft (20-27 N•m).
Repeat steps 1 through 5 for opposite side.
Manually rotate crankshaft (8) two complete revolutions to ensure free movement of lifters (3).

steps.text: Install head gasket (11) over dowel pins (12) on cylinder block (7).

notes.text: Head gasket must be used without sealer. Additional sealant may cause leaks or damage to engine.

steps.text: Clean threads of capscrews (10) with a wire brush to remove old pipe sealing compound. Apply pipe sealing compound to threads and under heads of capscrews (10).

notes.text: Use of cylinder head lifting device is optional. 1.1. Install cylinder head lifting device on center of cylinder head (9) with two washers (10.2) and capscrews (10.1). 1.2. Install cylinder head (9) on cylinder block (7) and remove two capscrews (10.1), washers (10.2), and cylinder head lifting device.

steps.text: Install cylinder head (9) on cylinder block (7) with seventeen capscrews (10). Tighten capscrews (10) to 20 lb-ft (27 N•m), following torque sequence shown.

notes.text: Failure to tighten cylinder head capscrews in proper sequence may result in leaks or damage to cylinder head.

steps.text: For 6.2 L engine, tighten seventeen capscrews (10) to 50 lb-ft (68 N•m), following torque sequence shown. 4.1 For 6.5 L engine, tighten seventeen capscrews (10) to 55 lb-ft (75 N•m), following torque sequence shown. 4.2 For 6.5 L engine, retighten seventeen capscrews (10) to 55 lb-ft (75 N•m), following torque sequence shown.
Tighten seventeen capscrews (10) an additional 90°, following torque sequence shown and mark capscrews (10).
Repeat steps 1 through 5 for opposite side.

diagrams.alt: Exploded view of a cylinder head, head gasket and capscrews above the cylinder block, with an optional lifting device.
diagrams.credit: US Army technical manual TM 9-2815-237-34, page 2-173

steps.text: Install four glow plugs (2) into cylinder head (l). Using glow plug socket, tighten glow plugs (2) to 8-12 lb-ft (11-16 N•m).
Repeat step 1 for opposite side.

steps.text: Install four gaskets (3) and fuel injection nozzles (4) into cylinder head (1). Using injector nozzle socket, tighten fuel injection nozzles (4) to 44-60 lb-ft (60-81 N•m).
Install three hoses (6) on fuel injection nozzles (4) with six clamps (5).
Install cap (7) on rear fuel injection nozzle (4) with clamp (5).
Repeat steps 1 through 3 for opposite side.

procedures.title: Engine assembly from subassemblies
procedures.section: r. Rocker Arm Shaft and Pushrods

steps.text: Install eight pushrods (1) in proper location with marked end of pushrods (1) up. Make sure pushrods (1) are properly seated.

notes.text: Marked ends of pushrods must point up when installed or engine damage may result.

steps.text: Install two rocker arm and shaft assemblies (2) on cylinder head (6). Make sure pushrods (1) properly seat in rocker arms (3).
Secure rocker arm and shaft assemblies (2) with four retainers (4) and capscrews (5). Tighten capscrews (5) to 41 lb-ft (56 N•m).
Repeat steps 1 through 3 for opposite side.

diagrams.alt: Exploded view of a pushrod and rocker arm and shaft assembly above an engine with cylinder head.
diagrams.credit: US Army technical manual TM 9-2815-237-34, page 2-176

steps.text: Install rocker arm cover gasket (13) on lip of cover (12) and align with capscrew holes.

notes.text: G If applying sealant, perform step 2. Keep sealant out of capscrew holes. G If installing new rocker arm cover gaskets, perform step 1, then step 3. G Silicone sealant can be used with the gasket, but is not required.

steps.text: Apply a 1/16-in. (4 mm) bead of silicone sealant around sealing surface of rocker arm covers (11).
